caption:
#FBF Touro College of Osteopathic Medicine Harlem held its biannual free community health fair last week in the sunny, spacious Adam Clayton Powell Jr. State Office Building Plaza! 
 
TouroCOM students provided health and wellness testing, counseling and demos to hundreds of visitors, while the crowed was entertained by a choir from Mama! Foundation for the Arts. Testing was provided for blood pressure, glucose, cholesterol, prostate, podiatry, vision, vaccines, TB, hepatitis, and dental, along with counseling on mental health, exercise, and CPR techniques.
 
Visitors received healthy eating and skincare tips and demonstrations while enjoying giveaways from this year’s numerous community partners, which included FDNY; New York College of Podiatric Medicine/Touro University; Columbia College of Dental Medicine; Mt. Sinai Tisch Cancer Center and Prostate Clinic; Planned Parenthood; Housing Works; African Services Committee; LiveOnNY; and Lafont eyewear.
 
“Our biannual health fair is one of the most meaningful events of the year because it allows us to give back to Harlem in a tangible way. Hundreds of visitors received vital screenings, counseling, and education, all made possible through the partnership of our students and community organizations,” said Sonya Alam, OMS-II and Community Service Chair 2025. “We learn the importance of meeting people where they are and addressing health needs with compassion and collaboration. It’s inspiring to see so many people come together to promote wellness, and the experience continues to shape us as future physicians committed to service.”

SHS students on Long Island celebrated the Jewish New Year with a fun Rosh Hashanah event co-sponsored by JLSA (Jewish Law Student Association)! The event featured all things apple and honey. A law student opened the event with a shofar blowing, and Rabbi Fogel spoke to the importance of making our world a better place in the New Year! 🍎🍏🍯

caption:
Congrats to New York College of Podiatric Medicine Touro University for their two prize winning posters in two different categories at the American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA) National Conference in Dallas, TX last month!

In the student poster category, the research involved development of novel antimicrobial therapeutic approaches for chronic wounds using nitric oxide.  The winners were Disal Wickramasinghe, Monica Cambi, and Tehreem Syed, and faculty Eileen Chusid, Ph.D., Anthony Iorio, DPM, Kemal Yariz, Ph.D., and Paramita Basu, Ph.D.

In the large case study/series category, faculty and students from NYCPM and Touro College of Pharmacy were recognized for a meta-analysis study on resistance patterns in diabetic foot infections and their correlations with pathogen prevalence and comorbidities.  The winners were Oren Sadeh, DPM, Weiqi Li, PharmD, Emily Yang, Svetlana Lopata, DPM, Priyank Kumar, Ph.D., and Paramita Basu, Ph.D. The joint research project has been submitted for publication. 

Pictured at the conference are, L-R: Dr. Basu, Disal Wickramasinge, Tehreem Syed and Monica Cambi.

Congratulations to all the winners!

caption:
Touro School of Health Sciences (SHS) occupational therapy (OT) students Andrew Tyburski, Tsering Choephel, and Samantha Pepe, alongside SHS OT Assistant Professor Dr. Linda Rini, and fellow OT students Katie Wright and Suzen-Lee Carry, recently presented their research project titled, "Exploration for Student Need for a Peer-led Coaching Intervention to Facilitate College Success." 

Focused on developing the first phase of an OT-led peer coaching program for college students, the group first created a survey to enable students to define for themselves what elements of the college experience, for example academics or social life, they're struggling with. "The survey results will help us to develop a peer-led OT coaching program to address those unique needs. I think a program like this, run by fellow students, will be very helpful for other students seeking advice and guidance in overcoming challenges. I also think it will be an amazing training opportunity for OT students like me to get invaluable hands-on experience and learn skills we can use as future practitioners," said Tyburski.

Look out for the survey to be sent to students in Touro’s undergraduate division including the Lander Colleges and NYSCAS, as well as to students at the Graduate School of Education and the School of Health Sciences next month!

caption:
Congratulations to TouroCOM Harlem on its recent launch of “MedAchieve III”, an eight-week summer program for NYC high school students focused on research! The enrollees are all graduates of TouroCOM’s successful high school STEM programs MedAchieve I (“MedStart”) and MedAchieve II (“MedExcel”). 

The students are working with TouroCOM DO student mentors to develop projects based on the needs of the Harlem community. They meet in weekly seminars to learn from local scientists about their own research and paths to science. Topics range from engineering to cardiovascular research. 

“Early exposure to science is helpful when applying to college and pursuing a career in science,” said TouroCOM Associate Professor, Pharmacology and Assistant Director of Community Affairs Dr. Kamilah Ali, who developed the program out of her own love for research. Content includes an intro to research skills and knowledge building; conducting needs assessments in Harlem; literature reviews; developing topics and hypotheses; collecting and analyzing data; and presenting results.

Among the local organizations involved are BioBus, which works with children to high school students in under-resourced areas to learn and discover science; God’s Love We Deliver; Pillars; Perinatal Partnership of Manhattan; and Maria Solá Green Space (Bronx). 

Pictured are the high school students gathered with Dr. Ali and their DO mentors. 
Back row L-R, speaker Michelle Kim; Raiyan Hasnaen, senior at Manhattan Center for Science and Mathematics, studying zip code mapping of bodegas vs supermarkets for type 2 diabetes in NYC; Dr. Ali; DO student mentors Gabrielle Singh, Nya Evans and Alexa Wallace; Jack Cao, senior, Stuyvesant High School, researching the effects of particulate matter on the development of the fruit fly. Bottom row, kneeling L-R, Anika Haque, a senior at Manhattan Center for Science and Mathematics researching coding of herbal medicines; and Abigail Hua, Smith College freshman, who is researching the effects of climate change on survival of aloe plants.

 

Congratulations to the future scientists!

caption:
#TBT TouroCOM Harlem students were active participants at the recent opening of the 51st annual HARLEM WEEK, which offers two weeks of activities to celebrate the arts and culture, people, entertainment and history of Harlem. This year’s theme is “Celebrate Our Magic”.

The festivities kicked off with “NY City Senior Citizens Day” at the Adam Clayton Powell, Jr., State Office Building.  TouroCOM students provided health demonstrations and testing. The day also included performances, a “Demystifying Technology” panel, a Senior Citizen Hat Fashion Show, and prominent speakers, such as New York Attorney General Letitia James.

Pictured are OMS-II Lidia Hassen providing information after a blood pressure reading, and also with District 9 Councilman Dr. Yusef Salaam.  Also pictured are Kevin Yeung, OMS-II, taking a blood pressure reading, and Ms. James speaking to attendees.

caption: ✨ Student Spotlight ✨ Meet Jenna, a 2nd-year DPT student at Touro’s Manhattan campus who is gearing up for the NYC Marathon this November! 🏃‍♀️🎉“After completing the NYC Half Marathon in 2024, I dreamed of one day running the full NYC Marathon. When Touro announced the chance to volunteer in the finish line medical tent, I jumped at it, hoping to get a closer look at the magic behind the race. Through volunteering, I witnessed firsthand how different health professions came together to care for runners, and I even got to apply lessons from my very first semester of school. Learning hands-on skills alongside SPTs and DPTs was an experience I’ll never forget and one I recommend to anyone who gets the chance! This year, I’m beyond grateful not only that Touro secured a marathon spot, but that I get to represent Team Touro as the runner. Training is tough, but every mile brings me closer to November. I’m so excited to take on the challenge and cross that finish line!” When Jenna isn’t running around training or studying you can find her hanging with friends & family! Good luck, Jenna — we can’t wait to root you on!💪 #TeamTouro #NYCMarathon #StudentSpotlight
